text: REST APIs allow different software systems to communicate with each other over the internet. Good API design follows several best practices. First, endpoints should be simple and clearly named, so developers can understand them easily. Second, APIs should return correct HTTP status codes, such as 200 for success or 404 when a resource is not found. Third, clear documentation is essential because it helps other developers use your API without confusion. Finally, versioning is important, as it allows you to improve your API without breaking existing applications. By following these practices, you can build reliable APIs that developers enjoy working with.
